description: Real-vehicle CAN dataset from an autonomous GEM e6 platform with explicit threat-model clarification distinguishing diagnostic-port emulation and software-compromise attacks.

attack_capability_classes.emulation_method: Replay of legitimate Autoware→PACMod control messages

threat_model.design_rationale: PCAN-based injection is used as a controlled emulation of real diagnostic-port and maintenance-tool attacks, while Autoware-generated tampering represents software-compromise threats producing fully valid actuator commands.

collection_environment.location: North Carolina A&T State University, North Campus closed-loop track
collection_environment.justification: Stationary operation preserves authentic CAN timing and ECU behavior while ensuring experimental safety.

attack_scenarios.rationale: Injection rate exceeds native control loop frequency (~10–11 Hz), achieving arbitration dominance and full bus saturation.
attack_scenarios.effect: 100% CAN bus load; blocks all traffic including attacker injections

attack_scenarios.rationale: Matches native actuator control frequency, producing syntactically valid but malicious commands indistinguishable from legitimate traffic.
Frequency-aligned integrity attack targeting steering ECU with hardware-valid identifiers and payloads.

labeling_policy.principle: Labels assigned based on synchronized attack windows and payload/ID matching, independent of transmission direction.

reuse_note: Attack specifications allow replay or software-based emulation of identical patterns for remote-compromise IDS evaluation.
